Why This Tactic Works (The "Winner's Curse")  In finance and game theory, forcing a rival to overpay exploits the Winner's Curse—the tendency for the winning bidder in a competitive auction to exceed the asset's intrinsic value due to ego, strategic FOMO, or sunk-cost fallacy. Hedge funds engineer this by: • Asymmetric Risk: If the fund already owns shares (like Ackman in Allergan), a higher bid from a rival guarantees a payout. • Credible Threat: A fund must have enough capital so the rival believes the fund could actually close the deal if they don't raise their bid. • Breakup Protections: In distressed debt or bankruptcy sales, court-approved breakup fees (typically 2% to 4% of the deal value) turn a losing bid into a guaranteed return

This is another case where a third-party marketing or email platform, not the company's own systems, became the weak point. 🇲🇦 ⚠️ MOROCCO — SECURITY SERVICES DENY BREACH AFTER 70K "AGENT" RECORDS LEAKED ON TELEGRAM  A self-described hacking group has published a list on Telegram that it says contains personal data on more than 70,000 Moroccan security agents.  Morocco's national police (DGSN) and domestic intelligence agency (DGST) issued a joint statement denying "any intrusion into its security databases." They say the published data is "old data" taken from systems run by insurance companies and health and social-coverage bodies, not from security systems.  Neither the leak claim nor the official explanation has been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Even if the data did not come from police or intelligence systems, a list tying names to security personnel can be used for doxxing, harassment and targeted phishing against officers and their families. The statement does not say which insurers or coverage bodies were involved.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Morocco #DataLeak #LawEnforcement #Hacktivism #ThreatIntelligence

The actor claims the data includes: • 4M+ email addresses • 4M+ phone numbers • 1M+ records with bank details  No passwords or credentials are claimed. What has changed is that it now appears to be circulating openly, which widens the exposure. Researchers, students and grant holders should watch for phishing and bank-fraud attempts using CAPES branding. CAPES has not confirmed an incident.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Brazil #CAPES #Government #DataLeak #ThreatIntelligence
